methods.steps: File > Export As opens the GIF export dialog; tick As animation to keep a multi-layer image moving.
methods.limits: As animation is disabled when the image has only one layer.

methods.steps: gifsicle -O3 input.gif -o optimized.gif
methods.limits: -O3 tries several optimization methods and can occasionally enlarge a file.

methods.steps: magick input.gif rewritten.gif
methods.limits: Its manual shows the magick input output form for converting between formats.

methods.steps: In Developer Tools settings tick "Take a screenshot of the entire page", or run :screenshot --fullpage --filename page.png in the Web Console. Then run magick page.png page.gif.
methods.limits: Firefox documents the .png extension for the file name.

methods.steps: Open docked Chrome DevTools and its Command Menu. Type screenshot; choose Capture area screenshot and drag the desired region. Convert the downloaded screenshot with magick screenshot.png page.gif.
methods.limits: Selected-area screenshot rather than full-page capture; requires docked DevTools.

methods.steps: After navigation, await page.screenshot({ path: 'capture.png', fullPage: true }); then magick capture.png capture.gif
methods.limits: A scripted PNG capture followed by GIF encoding; no animation recording implied.

methods.steps: ffmpeg -i recording.m4a -vn -c:a flac recording.flac
methods.limits: -vn disables video; -map selects streams.

methods.steps: Install the optional FFmpeg library; File > Import > Audio; then File > Export Audio and choose FLAC as the format.
methods.limits: M4A import requires the optional FFmpeg library; the FLAC options set channels, sample rate, bit depth and level.

methods.steps: Add the M4A file, choose the FLAC encoder and start the conversion.
methods.limits: The site says it converts freely between M4A/AAC and FLAC and runs on Windows, macOS and Linux; it does not list menu steps.

methods.steps: ffmpeg -i concert.mp4 -vn -c:a flac concert.flac
methods.limits: Add -map 0:a:N to choose an audio stream when the file has several.

methods.steps: File > Import > Audio; then File > Export Audio; select FLAC and review export settings.
methods.limits: MP4 import requires the optional FFmpeg library; the FLAC options set channels, sample rate, bit depth and level.

methods.steps: Run VLC without its interface: -I dummy --sout "#transcode{acodec=flac}:std{mux=raw,dst=yourAudio.flac}" with the video file as input, ending with vlc://quit.
methods.limits: The wiki's example is a Windows command that reads an .mp4 file.

methods.steps: ffmpeg -i archive.mpeg -vn -c:a pcm_s16le archive.wav
methods.limits: -vn disables video; -map selects streams.

methods.steps: With the optional FFmpeg library installed, File > Import > Audio; then File > Export Audio and choose WAV.
methods.limits: The manual says FFmpeg imports audio from most video files that are not DRM-protected; it does not name MPEG.

methods.steps: Run VLC without its interface: -I dummy --sout "#transcode{acodec=s16l,channels=2}:std{access=file,mux=wav,dst=yourAudio.wav}" with the video file as input, ending with vlc://quit.
methods.limits: The wiki's example is a Windows command that reads an .mp4 file; VLC's feature list names MPEG streams as input.

methods.steps: Develop the NEF; in the export module choose target storage: file on disk and file format: PNG; press start export.
methods.limits: darktable's features page lists PNG export and NEF import; it gives no camera list here.

methods.steps: magick photograph.nef photograph.png
methods.limits: The formats page lists NEF as read-only and PNG as read and write.

methods.steps: Select the photograph; NX Studio toolbar Export > Export as TIFF (8 Bit) or TIFF (16 Bit); open the TIFF in GIMP; File > Export As, export as PNG.
methods.limits: Two-stage method; NX Studio's export formats are JPEG, TIFF and HEIF, not PNG.

methods.steps: File > Export; File Format: PNG; choose Save Every Slide or Save Current Slide Only; set image size; export.
methods.limits: The page gives PNG as an example format; image size is set in the Width and Height boxes.

methods.steps: Open the deck in Impress; File > Export; select PNG as the file type; set PNG compression and interlacing.
methods.limits: The export page covers graphics file types and does not describe slide selection.

methods.steps: Drag the deck onto the Keynote icon to open it; File > Export To > Images; select slides; select an image format; Export.
methods.limits: Keynote's page doesn't list the image formats.

methods.steps: Open the PSD through the Open dialog; File > Export As; pick SVG.
methods.limits: Photopea's own export, not this page's; the page doesn't say whether its SVG holds vector paths or a picture.

methods.steps: File > Import; select the SVG; Import; pick a scaling option in the Import SVG dialog; OK; click the page. Then File > Export; select Adobe Illustrator (AI) from the Save as type list; enter a name; Export.
methods.limits: The export page gives AI as an example output format; the supported-formats page lists both SVG and AI without saying which direction each supports.

methods.steps: magick artwork.svg artwork.gif
methods.limits: The formats page notes that SVG renders through Inkscape, RSVG or the internal MSVG renderer, and that GIF holds up to 256 palette entries.

methods.steps: Open the SVG in Inkscape; Shift + Ctrl + E for the Export PNG Image dialog; choose the export area and the pixel size under Image Size; name the file and Export. Open the PNG in GIMP; File > Export As; export as GIF.
methods.limits: In the GIF dialog the As animation option is disabled for a single layer; GIMP's GIF export is limited to 256 colors.
